constraint:
The brief, in your words (19 Oct 2026): a UI to connect multiple brokers and their APIs (Kite, Dhan, Groww, 5paisa…). Then: “I think that will fall under the holding page.”

So every direction lives on Holdings, which stops being a coming-soon page. Settings keeps Account and the market-data connections.

rows.title: Today · no broker can be connected
rows.note:
Drawn from the code as it stands on staging; the Holdings and Settings copy is the shipped copy.

• Brokers you can connect: 0. Settings connects Dhan and FRED, and Dhan is used only for NSE closes (market mood, the Research summary).
• Holdings in Maester: 0. /terminal/holdings is the crane coming-soon page.
• The contract allows two providers only: ConnectionProvider = 'dhan' | 'fred', a database check on the same two, and a list that is “always two items, Dhan first”.

What the research changes for every direction: every broker signs Maester out each day (Zerodha at 6:00, Upstox 3:30, Fyers 6:30, Dhan after 24 hours unless renewed, Angel One and ICICI at midnight). No retail broker gives a personal app a lasting read token, because of SEBI’s 2025 retail-algo rules. Static IPs are needed only to place orders, so reading holdings needs none.

Yardstick: brokers 0 → as many as you hold accounts with; holdings shown 0 → every share, with where it is held and when it was read.

rows.title: A · Accounts, then one table
rows.note:
The bet: your accounts are a ledger of their own at the top of Holdings, and below it one table of what you own across all of them.

• The accounts ledger says, for each broker, where it stands in words (“Signed out at 06:00”), when its holdings were last read, and the one thing to do. A signed-out broker’s button is the screen’s primary action.
• The holdings table is one row per company with “Held at: Zerodha 120 · Dhan 30”. A quantity read before the sign-out carries a mark and the time it was read; it is not dropped from the total and not shown as zero.
• Add a broker opens in place: the brokers grouped by how you sign in, then that broker’s form with numbered steps, the redirect URL to copy, and its key fields.

Cost: new holdings API and adapters (see the plan); HoldingsTable gains Held at; AccountsLedger and BrokerPicker are new.

Length: about 1.5 desktop screens with three accounts.

rows.title: B · Each account, its own ledger
rows.note:
The bet: you think in accounts, the way the brokers show them. Holdings is a stack of accounts, each with its own ledger, average cost and subtotal, under a strip that adds them up.

• The signed-out notice sits inside the account it belongs to, with its own Sign in button, and that account’s figures stay visible, dated.
• A company held in two accounts is said once at the foot (“HDFC Bank 150 shares: Zerodha 120, Dhan 30”) rather than merged.
• Empty, the page is the broker sheet: every broker, how you sign in, how long a sign-in lasts and what it costs, so the choice is made with the facts in view.

Cost: the same backend as A; average cost is per account, which is what the brokers report, so no cross-account cost is needed.

Length: grows with accounts, about 2.2 screens with three.

rows.title: C · The statement first
rows.note:
The bet: one document already lists every share in every demat account: the depository’s monthly consolidated account statement (CAS, from CDSL or NSDL). Start there, through the Documents pipeline you already have, and use broker APIs only for what changed since.

• Covers every broker, including ones with no API or a paid one (Groww), with no daily sign-in.
• Each row shows the statement’s quantity, the brokers’ quantity today, and what changed in words (“10 more since the statement”).
• The daily sign-out matters less: a broker that is signed out falls back to the statement, dated.

Cost: a CAS reader (casparser, MIT, Python, beside the extractor), a PAN prompt to open the locked PDF (used once, not kept), and reconciliation rules. The statement has holdings only, no transactions and no cost, so Cost and gain stay unknown for statement-only holdings.

Length: about 1.6 screens.

rows.title: In every direction · connecting a broker
rows.note:
The round trip: save the key, sign in on the broker’s page, come back, read. Then done, refused (with the fix), and disconnect asks first and keeps what was read, dated.

Kept once connected: the key’s last 4, when you signed in, when the broker will sign Maester out, the last read, and “Can it trade? No.”

shared:
In every direction:

• Dhan is the one broker with no daily sign-in: the token you saved in Settings is renewed while Maester runs, and the same token reads your Dhan holdings.
• Read only. Maester asks for holdings and positions, never places an order and needs no static IP.
• A broker that is signed out or failing keeps its last read, with its time. It is never zero and never quietly left out of the total.
• Values are quantity × Friday’s NSE close from your Dhan data, worked out in financial-engine-ts, not the broker’s own last price. Which price is said on the page.
• Keys are checked with the broker before they are kept, stored encrypted like the Dhan token, and shown only by their last 4.
• Brokers that sign in only with a PIN and an authenticator code (Angel One, Kotak Neo, Shoonya, Motilal Oswal) are listed as not offered, with the reason.
• No advice words, no colour for direction, Synthetic example on every mock figure.
sheet:
The broker facts behind the frames (full sources in docs/research/2026-10-19-broker-apis.md):

Zerodha · sign in on Zerodha’s page · until 6:00 next day · Personal plan free, holdings included
Dhan · the token saved in Settings, renewed by Maester’s worker on every market pass (24-hour tokens) · Trading API free; Data API ₹499/month
Upstox · sign in on Upstox’s page · until 3:30 next day · free · one app per account since 1 Apr 2026
Fyers · sign in on Fyers’ page · until 6:30 next day · Standard plan free
ICICI Direct (Breeze) · browser session key · 24 h or midnight · free
5paisa · sign in on 5paisa’s page · the day · cost not stated
Groww · approve the key daily in Groww Cloud · daily · ₹499/month, required
Angel One · client code + PIN + TOTP · until midnight · free (not confirmed)
Kotak Neo · TOTP + MPIN · not stated · free

Static IP: orders only, at every broker checked. The exception is Upstox’s one-year Analytics Token, whose Portfolio calls need a whitelisted IP.

CAS: one PDF per PAN, monthly when anything moved, locked with the PAN. Holdings only.
questions:
I’d pick A · Accounts, then one table: it answers the brief as asked (connect the brokers, see what you hold), keeps the daily sign-ins in one place, and B’s per-account view can come later as a filter. C is the bigger idea: it reframes the brief around the depository statement and makes daily sign-ins optional.

Open questions:

1. Dhan: one credential, kept in Settings and shown on Holdings as an account (as drawn), or move it to Holdings?
2. PIN-and-code brokers (Angel One, Kotak Neo): leave them out (as drawn), or let you type the PIN and today’s code each morning, used once and not kept?
3. Which brokers do you hold accounts with? Round 1 assumes Zerodha, Dhan and Groww; the build starts with yours.
